conflicts.about: MTPD: the grid (2025) gives 168 h by the method's rule, the draft says >168 h

sides.claim: 168 h (the method's rule over the grid, 2025)
sides.speaker: method

conflicts.why: The method derives the MTPD from the grid; the other figure is the thing to explain.

conflicts.about: RTO of one-off payments and salary transfers: narrative says more than 168 hours, the labelled recovery line says 72 hours.

sides.claim: The narrative in the same interview calls the RTO more than 168 hours.
sides.quote: The one-off payments and salary transfers process has an RTO (recovery time objective) of more than 168 hours, because it was classed as not critical for short process outages.
sides.speaker: Heike Brodersen

sides.claim: The labelled recovery line in the same interview sets the RTO at 72 hours.
sides.speaker: Heike Brodersen

conflicts.why: The explicitly labelled 'RTO:' line is the structured scored answer in the method's read-back format and sits inside the stated MTPD, so 72 h is carried and the narrative reading is discarded.

gaps.what: The interview names sub-steps — recording, checking, releasing and transmitting one-off payments and salary transfers, and reconciling payment data with the released payroll and master data — but the BIA activity list is fixed with the manager at step 1 and here holds one activity; the merge of these sub-steps into A1 has not been confirmed.
gaps.ask: Do you confirm that recording, checking, releasing, transmitting and reconciling all merge into the single BIA activity 'One-off payments and salary transfers', with the worst score per category and the tightest clock?

gaps.what: No RPO was stated for the activity itself; the proposed <1 h rests only on the SAP S/4HANA Finance system rating.
gaps.ask: How much payment data may be lost before the salary transfer run is compromised — is <1 h the right recovery point for the activity?
